Foiley 1.2 adds airfoil generators:
* NACA 4-digit, 5-digit (standard and reflexed), 4-digit modified,
  16-series, 6-series and 6A-series sections;
* CST, PARSEC, Kármán–Trefftz and cambered-plate sections.

The optimizer can now also vary CST weights.

## NACA families

Type a designation in **Foil design → Create**. You can also give one
anywhere a foil is accepted on the command line, such as
`foiley foil polar "NACA 64(2)-415"`, or use
`foiley foil gen naca "<code>"`.

- **5-digit, now complete:** reflexed mean lines (`23112`, 221xx to 251xx)
  and any design lift coefficient (first digit × 0.15: `13012`, `43012`).
  The reflexed moment about c/4 is nominally zero. NACA's rounded constants
  leave at most 0.0045 × design CL.
- **Closed trailing edge** for 4- and 5-digit sections (`2412 closed TE`):
  the x⁴ coefficient is −0.1036 instead of −0.1015.
- **4-digit modified** (`0012-64`, also with a 5-digit mean line such as
  `23015-64`) and **16-series** (`16-009`, `16-212`).
- **6-series** (`63-206`, `64(2)-415` or `64₂-415`, `65-415 a=0.5`; 63 to 67)
  and **6A-series** (`64A010`, `63A210`, `64(2)A215`), from NASA's
  conformal-mapping data.

Each family is built the way its NACA report defines it, with the thickness
perpendicular to the mean line.

**Compatibility with 1.1.**
- Every code XFoil's own `NACA` command accepts generates exactly what it
  did in 1.1 and in XFoil: any 1- to 4-digit code, and 210xx–250xx. All
  10,500 codes are checked bit for bit, and saved projects are not affected.
- 1.1's separator spellings still read as their digits: `24-12`, `23-012`,
  `NACA_24_12`.
- Trailing words are no longer dropped. `NACA 2412 mod` used to silently
  become plain NACA 2412; it is now an ordinary foil name.
- Report 824's older scaled notation (`65(318)-217`) is refused with an
  explanation rather than approximated.

## CST, PARSEC, Kármán–Trefftz and cambered plates

- **CST (Kulfan):**
  - Edit the weights with a live preview.
  - *Fit to selected foil* fits CST weights to a foil, including a loaded
    `.dat`, by least squares and reports the fit error. A fit whose surfaces
    would cross is refused with a suggestion to lower the order.
  - Command line: `foiley foil fit-cst FOIL --order 8 [--json]` and
    `foiley foil gen cst`.
- **PARSEC:** Sobieczky's 11 parameters (LE radius, crests, TE height,
  thickness, direction and wedge), solved per surface.
- **Kármán–Trefftz:** Joukowsky with a finite trailing-edge angle. The exact
  inviscid CL and Cm are shown next to the parameters
  (`foiley foil gen kt --exact 0,4`).
- **Cambered plates:** constant thickness, circular-arc or parabolic camber
  and a round leading edge, for very low Reynolds numbers.
  - The default trailing edge is cut square to the plate (`--te square`),
    which XFoil analyses.
  - A round trailing edge (`--te round`) is available for geometry, but
    XFoil's viscous solution does not converge on it.

Generated foils keep their recipe. **Edit parameters** reopens it, and
**Replace selected** applies a new shape to an existing foil while keeping
its name and hinge.

**Shapes that are refused.** Generators reject parameters whose contour
crosses itself or encloses no area. For CST and PARSEC, positive thickness
is proven exactly in the Bernstein basis, not sampled.

**AVL export.** It writes a native `NACA` line only when the foil's
coordinates are that section; a foil reshaped under a NACA name is exported
as a file. Each foil gets its own flat, portable file name.

## Optimizer

Under **Shape variables**, choose **CST weights** instead of Hicks–Henne
bumps (`foiley foil optimize --shape cst --cst-order 5`). The genes are
changes of the CST weights added to the base foil. Each gene changes
thickness, camber or the LE radius over the whole chord, without local
waviness.

**Changes to existing behaviour.**
- The base foil is still moved and scaled to unit chord with its leading
  edge at the origin, but it is no longer rotated, for both kinds of genes.
  Zero genes keep its angle of attack. Before, a foil whose leading edge is
  not its leftmost point was analysed slightly rotated.
- Settings saved by 1.1 load as Hicks–Henne.

## Command line and Studio

- **Output protection.** Outputs that would overwrite the input project,
  another output, or a recipe file are refused. That includes hard links,
  and links or junctions created while a command runs. Files are written
  through a temporary file and a rename.
- **Inverse design in Studio.** Inverse-design results and every Modify
  preview are tied to the foil and geometry they came from, and are dropped
  when another foil is selected or added, or after an edit, undo or redo. A
  speed distribution is also tied to its mode, angle and paneling.
- **`.dat` titles.** A title that reads as numbers, such as `10 10`, is
  written in quotes so it reads back as the title.

## Checks

| Item | Check |
|---|---|
| 5-digit (incl. reflexed), 4-digit modified, 16-, 6- and 6A-series match NASA's NACA4/NACA6 ordinates within 1.6e-5 c aft of x/c 0.0125 (5-decimal tables; up to 1.9e-4 c at the nose) | `naca_reference.rs` |
| All 10,500 codes XFoil accepts are bit-identical to 1.1; 1.1 separator spellings still read | `every_code_xfoil_accepts_is_unchanged`, `foiley_1_1_separator_spellings_still_read`, `foiley_1_1_labels_still_resolve` |
| LE index 9 is three times the normal radius; Report 824 scaled notation and `a` just below 1 are refused | `le_index_9_is_three_times_the_normal_radius`, `report_824_scaled_notation_is_refused_with_its_reason`, `mean_line_parameter_near_one_is_refused_and_literals_are_kept` |
| Reflexed mean lines have a nominally zero thin-airfoil Cm about c/4 (within 2e-3 at design CL 0.3) | `reflexed_mean_line_has_zero_moment` |
| Positive thickness is proven exactly (Bernstein subdivision); crossings between stations, coincident surfaces, folding or hooked plates, PARSEC troughs and runaway surfaces, and unsupported CST inputs are rejected | `bernstein_positivity_is_exact`, `coincident_and_between_station_crossings_are_rejected`, `crossing_contours_are_found`, `folding_plates_are_rejected`, `bad_parameters_are_rejected`, `unsupported_class_exponents_and_inverted_edges_are_rejected` |
| ± camber plates are exact mirror images with sane properties, and converge mirrored from 0° to 3° at Re 1e5 | `both_camber_signs_give_mirrored_sections_and_sane_properties`, `every_family_converges_in_a_viscous_analysis` |
| The exact Kármán–Trefftz moment (Blasius) matches a 400,000-point pressure integration; XFoil's inviscid CL is within 0.3% and Cm within 4e-4 | `blasius_moment_matches_a_converged_pressure_integral`, `karman_trefftz.rs` |
| One section per family converges in a viscous analysis | `every_family_converges_in_a_viscous_analysis` |
| CST fits (NACA 2412 order 8: max 2e-4 c), exact recovery of CST weights, refused crossing fits | `fitting_naca_sections_is_accurate`, `a_fit_of_a_cst_foil_recovers_its_weights`, `a_fit_that_would_cross_is_refused_and_lower_orders_regenerate` |
| PARSEC surfaces meet all 11 conditions | `the_surfaces_meet_every_condition` |
| Optimizer: zero genes give the base foil in its own frame; invalid settings are input errors, not panics; 1.1 settings load | `cst_genes_change_the_shape_smoothly`, `optim_zero_genes_is_base` |
| AVL export uses `NACA` only for foils that are that section and gives each foil its own safe file | `a_foil_reshaped_under_a_naca_name_is_exported_as_a_file`, `foils_whose_file_names_collide_get_their_own_files` |
| Recipes round-trip through projects; numeric `.dat` titles round-trip; absurd coordinates are rejected | `recipes_round_trip_through_json`, `recipes_survive_a_project_round_trip`, `numeric_titles_round_trip_and_huge_counts_do_not_panic` |
| Clippy gate passes | `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings` |

## Known limit

**What fails.** Thin 6-series sections with a high design CL on the a = 1.0
mean line, such as NACA 63-406, end in a near-cusped, hooked trailing edge.
XFoil's sharp-trailing-edge condition then gives a wrong inviscid solution;
it does the same with NASA's own ordinates.

**Workarounds.** Add a 0.05% TE gap (*Modify → TE gap*) or use an a < 1
mean line. 63-206, 63-412, 64(2)-415, 65-610 and 66-209 solve normally.
